title: Manager succession onboarding kit (21/60/120) — lateral manager conversions (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a living playbook for converting high-performing ICs or senior individual contributors into first-time or lateral managers. Designed for use by People Ops, hiring managers, and the receiving team. Focus: reduce time-to-impact, surface early coaching signals, and create a repeatable cadence for 21/60/120 checkpoints.

Status: WIP. Use this as the operational checklist and interview/rubric adjustments when we consider internal lateral promotions or external hires into manager roles that require quick team transition.

High-level assumptions:
- Candidate may already know product and some teammates.
- Role may require immediate run-rate (people processes, performance calibration) within 60 days.
- Manager will be given a 4-week ramp window with protected focus for org/1:1 setup.

Pre-offer / pre-boarding checklist (People Ops + Hiring Manager):
- Confirm scope: direct reports, matrix relationships, hiring authority, compensation band signoff (JIRA-PEOPLE-482).
- Update role doc and 30/60/90 deliverables in job spec.
- Schedule a 30-min pre-boarding call (manager + manager's manager + People Ops) for role clarity.
- Create onboarding folder with team goals, current roadmap, OKRs, and cross-functional RACI.
- Snapshot of direct reports: tenure, current performance signals, ongoing 1:1 cadence, active performance plans.
- Slack introductions draft + suggested first-day agenda.
- Access provisioning checklist: GH teams, internal wiki, payroll, HRIS, calendar delegation.

Day 0-7 (first week) — immediate priorities:
- Day 0: Welcome + hardware check, HR paperwork, intro note in #team channel.
- Day 1: 1:1 with manager (90m) — share role expectations, immediate priorities, escalation paths.
- Day 2–3: Discovery syncs with each direct report (30m each) using "get-to-know" template (see template below).
- Day 4: Kick off operational owners review (on-call, deploy leads, release cadence).
- Day 5: Ask for first-week reflection in onboarding doc.

21-day checkpoint (focus: situational awareness + early wiring):
- Deliverable: manager submits a 21-day org wiring note: team map, top 3 risks, top 3 opportunities, proposed immediate changes.
- Meeting: 1:1 with manager's manager to align on expectations and course-correct.
- People Ops: review initial signals from direct reports (anonymized pulse if requested).
- Success signals: has run introductory 1:1s, updated team docs, understands major deliverables and blockers.
- Red flags: no 1:1s scheduled, unclear owner mapping, unaddressed urgent people issues.

60-day checkpoint (focus: team rhythms + small wins):
- Deliverable: 60-day plan with hiring needs, process changes, measurable small win (e.g., stabilized sprint cadence, removed a recurring blocker).
- Manager should complete at least one meaningful people action (e.g., resolved a team conflict, led a retro action, closed a hiring scorecard).
- People Ops: check in on manager capability gaps and recommend a 1:1 coaching plan or cohort.

120-day checkpoint (focus: sustained impact and growth plan):
- Deliverable: 120-day review doc including hiring plan, career paths, 6-month org OKRs.
- Performance calibration: prepare evidence packets for manager's decision-making on promotions or performance plans.
- Success signals: team metrics moving in desired direction, stable 1:1 cadence, documented hiring pipeline.

Interview rubric adjustments (when hiring externally into a lateral manager role):
- Eval axes (each scored 1-5 with evidence):
  - People leadership: examples of coaching, feedback cycles, and talent development.
  - Decision-making: tradeoffs, escalation judgment, and cross-team negotiation.
  - Operational fluency: familiarity with delivery processes relevant to the team (sprint cadence, release, incident playbooks).
  - Domain competence: technical/product context sufficient to mentor ICs.
  - Cultural fit & communication: clarity with stakeholders, cross-functional empathy.
- Calibration notes: emphasize behavioral examples (not hypotheticals). Ask for a specific case where candidate changed a process and what the metrics were.

Sample interview prompts (people ops + hiring manager use):
- "Tell me about a time you coached an engineer who was high-performing technically but struggling with cross-team communication. What was your approach and outcome?"
- "Describe a decision where you chose to delay a feature to protect long-term quality. How did you communicate that to stakeholders?"
- "Give a concrete example where you restructured work allocation on your team to improve throughput. What measurement did you use?"

Manager 1:1 template (initial three sessions):
- Session 1 (intro): priorities, past wins, blockers, expectations for 1:1, signals that indicate success.
- Session 2 (week 2): recap of week 1, career aspirations, development areas, immediate blockers.
- Session 3 (week 3): 21-day wiring feedback, adjust cadence, set first measurable goal.

Onboarding evidence journal (quick template):
- Date | Interaction | Signal (positive/negative) | Action taken | Owner | Follow-up date
- Use for rapid collection of coaching, trust signals, and early risk.

Training & support catalog (suggested, not exhaustive):
- Mandatory: Manager fundamentals cohort (monthly, 6 sessions).
- Strongly recommended: Feedback and calibration workshop (quarterly).
- Optional: Technical mentoring clinic (peer-run), Performance management deep-dive (as needed).

People Ops operations for manager conversions (checklist):
- Confirm promotion/comp paperwork and compensation mapping.
- Prepare org chart and updated JD in HRIS.
- Schedule skip-level 30-day coffee (manager's manager invites cross-functional partners).
- Offer curated learning path + budget (first 90 days).
- Decide on probation signals (if applicable) and review cadence.

Open questions / items to resolve (notes to self):
- Do we want a separate "internal lateral" calibration track for salary bands? (dependent on comp team).
- Should people-ops auto-schedule a 30-day skip-level on behalf of the manager? Pros/cons.
- Pilot: create a 6-person cohort for managers converted from ICs in Q4 2025 — measure NPS + time-to-first-hire.

Related artifacts and quick links: JIRA-PEOPLE-482 (promotion flow), RFC: manager-1:1-template-v2 (Confluence), GH: hr-onboarding-templates/pull/58 (starter docs).

Quick templates (copy-paste):
- First-week intro message (Slack): "Hi team — excited to introduce [Name], stepping into [Role]. They'll be focusing on [x] and running 1:1s starting this week. Please add notes to the shared onboarding doc: <link>."

- 21-day wiring note header:
  - Team map: (list)
  - Top 3 risks and mitigations:
  - Top 3 quick wins:
  - Immediate hiring needs:

Implementation notes: keep this doc light and operational. People Ops to own versioning and measurements (NPS post-60-day, manager + direct report pulse). Add examples from pilot hires to the appendix as we iterate.

Last edited by: Aisha Patel — notes: pushing pilot in Q4; avatars for manager cohorts coming from Learning Ops.
